messages.author: dcaf23790c09a94d
messages.subject: Using ranef on stacked data
parts:
Hello,

I am using gdistsamp to determine detection probabilities and densities for line transect surveys. I ended up stacking the data and was able to get a set of models to fit the data and pass the GoF test (top model). My question now - can I use ranef on stacked data? If so, what are the units of the output? Is it abundance or density (I specify density in the model)? The reason I ask is that is when I use the backTransform function on the top model, I get a reasonable density for each site for a given year, but the ranef results are very high in comparison. I did a general "ranef" search on the forum, but couldn't come up with an answer. Any suggestions/input is appreciated. Thanks!

Cheers,
Tim Schreckengost
Master's Candidate
Department of Entomology and Wildlife Ecology
University of Delaware

messages.author: 4a15de51da4445ae
messages.subject: Re: [unmarked] Using ranef on stacked data
parts:
hi Tim,
 it's hard to say what's going on here.
 I think the scale of the random effects predictinos and the backtransformed linear predictor should be the same.
 I think your K is set too small here.  In addition it's possible that with a lot of over-dispersion the back-transformation of the linear predictor isn't giving very sensible point estimates and so may not be that meaningful.
 For example, think of the log-normal situation with y ~ lognormal(mu, sigma2), the E(y) is not exp(mu) but rather exp(mu + .5*sigma2) and exp(mu) will in general be much less than the mean of the random variable.
 I'm just babbling here but I think in general you may not have a close correspondance between the exp(mu) and predictions of individual N's.
regards
andy
